Body.Content:
What and why

We’re improving the backup and restore experience in Microsoft Authenticator for Android. When setting up Authenticator on a new device, users will receive guidance tailored to whether they still have access to their previous device. They will also receive guidance on using Authenticator passkeys for cross-device sign-in. This experience is already available on iOS.

To use backup and restore on a new Android device, users must enable Google One backup and screen lock.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in mid-January 2027 and expected to complete in mid-January 2027

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Users of Microsoft Authenticator on Android

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Authenticator for Android

What will happen

  • When setting up Authenticator on a new Android device, users will see clearer guidance based on whether they still have access to their previous device.
  • Users will receive guidance for using Authenticator passkeys for cross-device sign-in.
  • Work or school accounts are not backed up. This is not changing.
  • Backup will continue to support TOTP credentials for Microsoft personal accounts and third-party accounts.
  • Users must enable Google One backup and screen lock to use this backup and restore experience.
  • Backup and restore is supported only when Microsoft Authenticator is installed in the Android personal profile. It is not supported when Authenticator is installed in an Android work profile.

Action required and recommendations

No admin action is required.

Organizations may choose to inform users about the updated restore experience on Android devices.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

Title: Microsoft Authenticator: Improved backup and restore experience for Android
